subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should `clawhub skill publish` use for publisher-declared GitHub source metadata?
rationale: The code intentionally protects the trusted provenance boundary, but only maintainers can decide whether unverified attribution belongs in the public product, whether CLI publishes should perform stronger server verification, or whether the currently ambiguous flags should be removed.

options.title: Separate Unverified Attribution
options.body: Retain and expose the declared repository metadata under an unmistakably unverified field while keeping verification and trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

options.title: Verify CLI Sources
options.body: Add a server-controlled workflow that verifies repository access, commit identity, source path, and uploaded-content equivalence before recording trusted provenance.

options.title: Deprecate Source Flags
options.body: Stop accepting or deprecate the flags and clearly document that ordinary CLI publishing cannot create GitHub-backed provenance.

recommendation.title: Separate Unverified Attribution
recommendation.body: Retain and expose the declared repository metadata under an unmistakably unverified field while keeping verification and trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source work established the adjacent trust model and makes them the strongest history-based routing candidate.
